niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a psychology-oriented approach, a guided spiritual tradition, or a mix. These are good starting points from the options I found:

### Shadow work
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A focused, Jungian-oriented course with video and audio lessons and practical exercises. A strong pick if you want shadow work grounded in depth psychology rather than a general self-help program.
- **[Shadow Work Course and Workbook — Udemy](https://www.udemy.com/course/shadow-work-course/)** — A lower-commitment, self-paced option with a workbook. Check the current syllabus and instructor background before enrolling.
- **[Do Your Own Shadow Work: Beginning to Advanced Practices — Udemy](https://www.udemy.com/course/shadow-work-x/)** — Offers a range of practices and may suit learners who prefer a broad, self-guided format. Its approach includes spiritual elements, so review the course description to see if that fits you.

### Spiritual practice
- **[Essentials of Engaged Contemplation — Center for Action and Contemplation](https://cac.org/living-school/essentials-of-engaged-contemplation-course/)** — A fully online course for developing contemplative practice, with a Christian contemplative orientation.
- **[Ananda Course in Meditation](https://www.ananda.org/online-courses/)** — A structured 10-week course for building a regular meditation practice, rooted in Ananda’s spiritual tradition.
- **[Spirituality & Practice e-courses](https://www.spiritualityandpractice.com/ecourses/course)** — A directory of online courses and retreats across different traditions; useful if you want to compare approaches.

**My short recommendation:** Try Jung Platform for shadow work and Ananda or the Center for Action and Contemplation for a more structured spiritual practice. If you want a secular approach, check the course’s teachings and exercises carefully before signing up.

Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions. A course is not a substitute for therapy; consider working with a qualified mental-health professional if the material feels overwhelming or connects to trauma. Prices, availability, and course details can change, so verify them on the provider’s site.
